proofs.proof_tex:
By the established design-A nonemptiness criterion,
\[
 \mathcal F_A(p,m)\ne\varnothing
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 m\in\Delta_{\mathcal E}^{\circ}
 \ \text{and}\ 
 \mathcal C_A(T)\ne\varnothing. \tag{1}
\]
Thus failure of the observable strict-margin test is incompatibility, even if the normalized cycle equations alone happen to have a solution.  For design B, surjectivity in the established cycle-to-SCM lift gives
\[
 \mathcal F_B(p)\ne\varnothing
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \mathcal C_B(T)\ne\varnothing. \tag{2}
\]
In particular, an empty full fiber has an empty target image and is not rigid under the cardinality-one definition.

After the margin test in design A, let \(X=\mathcal C_A(T)\); in design B let \(X=\mathcal C_B(T)\).  The simplex equalities, nonnegativity or strict-positivity signs, factorization equations, response-level shared-\(Z\) equations, and the finite disjunction expressing relevance show directly from the cycle-fiber definition that \(X\) is a bounded semialgebraic set over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\).  The map
\[
 f(x)=\tau_C(x)=
 \left(\sum_z a_{11,2}(z),\sum_z a_{00,2}(z)\right) \tag{3}
\]
is polynomial.  Apply the established one-sample/all-chart rigidity lemma to the one-element family \(X_1=X\).  If the sampling call reports emptiness, (1) or (2) proves incompatibility.  Otherwise it returns \(x_0\in X\); put \(t_0=f(x_0)\).  The lemma's only refinement is
\[
 R(x_0)=X\cap\left\{x:
 (f_1(x)-t_{0,1})^2+(f_2(x)-t_{0,2})^2>0
 \right\}. \tag{4}
\]
If \(R(x_0)=\varnothing\), every \(x\in X\) has \(f(x)=t_0\), so \(f(X)=\{t_0\}\).  Conversely, if \(f(X)=\{t_0\}\), no point satisfies the strict inequality in (4).  Hence the single refinement is empty if and only if the target image of the raw fiber is a singleton.

The cycle-to-SCM lift is onto and target preserving, so
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathcal T_A(p,m)
 &=\{\tau_C(b,a):(b,a)\in\mathcal C_A(T)\},\\
 \mathcal T_B(p)
 &=\{\tau_C(b,a):(b,a,m,g,\pi)\in\mathcal C_B(T)\}.
 \end{aligned} \tag{5}
\]
Combining (4) and (5) proves the asserted necessary-and-sufficient causal rigidity test.  If (4) is nonempty, its sampled point \(x_1\) satisfies \(f(x_1)\ne f(x_0)\).  Lift \(x_0\) and \(x_1\) separately by the cycle-to-SCM lemma.  The two lifts lie in the same full fiber, hence have identical selected observables and, in design A, the same supplied margin, while target preservation gives different values of \(\tau\).  These are the required legal twins.  If both cycle points lie in interior support charts, the established positive-lift lemma makes every response mass, proxy and instrument kernel, treatment probability, and selection probability strictly interior.  That lemma makes no positivity assertion for a boundary-face witness, exactly as required.

The effective semialgebraic sampling result represents \(x_0\) by a real-univariate representation with Thom signs over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\).  Since (3) is linear in its cycle coordinates, \(t_0\) belongs to the finite real algebraic field generated by that representation.  The second call is made over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0)\) and, when nonempty, returns the same exact type of representation for \(x_1\).  A rational expression over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\) is returned only when the field computation constructs one.  Otherwise a square-free real-univariate polynomial, rational coordinate functions, and Thom signs select the ordered real value exactly.  For rational input, clearing the guarded observable denominators and applying square-free factorization and real-root isolation give an integer polynomial and rational isolating data.  Thus all exact-output clauses follow.  The exhaustive structural atlas may attach a diagnostic label afterward, but neither the proof of (4) nor the mandatory computation enumerates a chart or a connected component.

Condition 1 of Shingaki--Yoshida--Kuroki has the selected-law factorization
\[
 p(x,y,s,w,z,u)
 =p(s\mid x,y)p(y\mid x,u)p(x\mid z,u)
   p(w\mid u)p(z\mid u)p(u). \tag{6}
\]
Response consistency makes \(p(y\mid x,u)\) the deterministic kernel encoded by the four response types.  Outcome-dependent selection supplies \(p(s\mid x,y)\), proxy exclusion supplies \(p(w\mid u)\), and the treatment, second-proxy, and response-type mechanisms in \(P_{\vartheta}\) supply the remaining factors.  Hence, at the selected-law factorization level, \(\mathfrak M\) is the finite four-response-type specialization of that condition.

The design-A definition adds
\[
 P_{\vartheta}(E,W,Z\mid S=1)=p,
 \qquad P_{\vartheta}(E)=m. \tag{7}
\]
Thus \(\mathcal F_A(p,m)\) is the subfiber obtained by fixing the population cell margins.  On a compatible member satisfying the published regular Conditions 2--3, the cited regular-identification result applies pointwise.  If \(R_A(p)\) denotes the pair computed by Appendix equations (A.28)--(A.33), that result gives
\[
 \tau(\vartheta)=R_A(p)
 \quad\text{for every }\vartheta\in\mathcal F_A(p,m). \tag{8}
\]
Compatibility makes the fiber nonempty, and therefore
\[
 \mathcal T_A(p,m)=\{R_A(p)\}. \tag{9}
\]
The full-rigidity theorem returns the unique element of this target set.  This is transfer by restriction: fixing \(m\) cannot alter a conclusion valid for every member of the larger regular fiber.

For design B, instrument exogeneity changes the last two factors in (6) to
\(p(z\mid u)p(u)=g(z)p(u)\).  Every member consequently obeys
\[
 p(x,y,s,w,z,u)
 =p(s\mid x,y)p(y\mid x,u)p(x\mid z,u)
   p(w\mid u)g(z)p(u), \tag{10}
\]
which is equation (13) of the cited paper.  The definition of \(\mathcal F_B(p)\) additionally imposes instrument relevance.  On a compatible law satisfying Conditions 2--3, the cited regular IV identification result applies directly to (10).  Writing its observable answer as \(R_B(p)\),
\[
 \tau(\vartheta)=R_B(p)
 \quad\text{for every }\vartheta\in\mathcal F_B(p),
 \qquad
 \mathcal T_B(p)=\{R_B(p)\}. \tag{11}
\]
The full-rigidity theorem again returns this unique value.

Equations (8) and (11) have only the published regular scope.  Outside it, the mixed-support theorem exhausts rank-two orientations, rank-one \(\mathrm L,\mathrm R,\mathrm E,\mathrm D\) modes, all coefficient-support faces, shared endpoints, and, in design B, every residual-forest and active-cycle state.  The full-rigidity theorem then reports incompatibility for an empty full fiber and, on every compatible singular or boundary law, returns either the exact common target or legal target-changing SCM twins.  This is a classification extension on compatible singular and boundary fibers; it neither extends the published regular formula beyond its hypotheses nor asserts blanket subsumption.

On the stated experimental submodel, \(S=1\) almost surely implies \(m=r\), and \(X\perp(U,W,Z)\) implies \(P(U=i\mid X=x)=\pi_i\).  The cited Shingaki--Kuroki result, under its displayed Conditions (1)--(3), identifies the four response-type probabilities and supplies the consistent plug-in estimator used here.  We verify that the same observable restrictions also make the design-A cycle target rigid.

Fix \(e=(x,y)\) with \(\mathcal I_e=\{i,j\}\), and for a proxy category \(w\) form
\[
 \widetilde Q_{ew}=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 1&P(W=w\mid E=e)\\
 P(Z=z_1\mid E=e)&P(W=w,Z=z_1\mid E=e)
 \end{pmatrix}. \tag{12}
\]
The matrix used in the cited construction differs only by positive cell-probability normalizations.  Substitution of
\(T_e=b_i a_{ei}^{\top}+b_j a_{ej}^{\top}\) into (12) and expansion of the two products give
\[
 \det(\widetilde Q_{ew})
 =K_e\{b_i(w)-b_j(w)\},
 \qquad
 K_e=a_{ei}(z_1)A_{ej}-A_{ei}a_{ej}(z_1), \tag{13}
\]
where \(A_{eh}=\sum_z a_{eh}(z)\).  The determinant nonvanishing and determinant-ratio separation required in Condition (3), together with the nonsingular systems in equations (8)--(11), imply \(K_e\ne0\), \(b_i\ne b_j\), and distinct incident directions at every response type.  Therefore every \(T_e\) has rank two, its determinant ratios identify the direction of \(\mathcal L_e\), and the two incident lines identify the common endpoint \(b_i\) uniquely.

The established rank-two orientation atlas is exhaustive.  Once each shared endpoint is the unique intersection just obtained, every nonempty oriented endpoint interval is a singleton.  For any coordinate \(h\) with \(b_i(h)\ne b_j(h)\), the factorization equations then give
\[
 a_{ei}(z)=v_e(z)
 \frac{c_{ez}(h)-b_j(h)}{b_i(h)-b_j(h)},
 \qquad
 c_{ez}=\frac{T_e(\cdot,z)}{v_e(z)}, \tag{14}
\]
and \(a_{ej}(z)=v_e(z)-a_{ei}(z)\).  Positivity of the observed cells makes \(v_e(z)>0\), so all divisions used in (14) are legal.  Thus every point of the cycle fiber has the same target as the generating experimental SCM.

Under \(\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}=(\pi_4,\pi_2,\pi_3,\pi_1)\), response consistency and randomization give
\[
 \mathrm{PN}
 =\frac{\pi_2}{\pi_1+\pi_2}
 =\frac{\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}_2}
        {\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}_2+\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}_4},
 \qquad
 \mathrm{PS}
 =\frac{\pi_2}{\pi_2+\pi_4}
 =\frac{\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}_2}
        {\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}_1+\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}_2}. \tag{15}
\]
The denominators are positive because the corresponding observed cells are positive.  Equations (13)--(15), the rank-two atlas, and the target-preserving lift prove
\[
 \mathcal T_A(p,r)=\{\phi_{\mathrm{SK}}(\pi^{\mathrm{SK}})\}. \tag{16}
\]
The exact compiler must return this singleton.  Consistency from the cited experimental identification result and continuity of \(\phi_{\mathrm{SK}}\) at the positive denominators in (15) yield
\[
 \phi_{\mathrm{SK}}(\widehat\pi_n^{\mathrm{SK}})
 \xrightarrow{P}\phi_{\mathrm{SK}}(\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}). \tag{17}
\]

We next verify the displayed boundary datum.  Every \(b_i^{\mathrm{bd}}\) is strictly positive and sums to one.  In each cell, the two coefficient rows are nonnegative, sum coordinatewise to \((1/3,1/3,1/3)\), and are not proportional.  The two incident endpoints are distinct probability vectors and hence are linearly independent.  Consequently
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(T_e^{\mathrm{bd}})=2
 \quad(e\in\mathcal E). \tag{18}
\]
For every \((w,z)\), at least one incident coefficient is positive and both endpoint coordinates are positive; hence all entries of \(T_e^{\mathrm{bd}}\), and therefore of \(p^{\mathrm{bd}}\), are positive.  Moreover
\[
 \sum_e s_e^{\mathrm{bd}}m_e^{\mathrm{bd}}
 =\frac14\left(\frac18+\frac14+\frac38+\frac12\right)
 =\frac5{16},
 \qquad
 \frac{s_e^{\mathrm{bd}}m_e^{\mathrm{bd}}}{5/16}
 =r_e^{\mathrm{bd}} \tag{19}
\]
for every cell.  Thus the displayed cycle point and selection law obey the required normalization, and the cycle-to-SCM lift proves
\(\mathcal F_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})\ne\varnothing\).

Direct substitution in simplex coordinates gives
\[
 \mathcal L_{11}=\mathcal L_{00}
 =\{b:b(w_2)=1/5\},
 \qquad
 \mathcal L_{01}=\{b:b(w_1)=1/5\},
 \qquad
 \mathcal L_{10}=\{b:b(w_3)=1/5\}. \tag{20}
\]
The transverse intersections in (20) fix \(b_1^{\mathrm{bd}},b_3^{\mathrm{bd}},b_4^{\mathrm{bd}}\).  In cell \(11\), the normalized columns at \(z_1,z_3\) are \(b_1^{\mathrm{bd}},b_2^{\mathrm{bd}}\), so the segment constraint puts the type-\(2\) endpoint on the ray from \(b_2^{\mathrm{bd}}\) away from \(b_1^{\mathrm{bd}}\).  In cell \(00\), the corresponding columns are \(b_2^{\mathrm{bd}},b_4^{\mathrm{bd}}\), so the same endpoint lies on the ray from \(b_2^{\mathrm{bd}}\) away from \(b_4^{\mathrm{bd}}\).  The strict order on their common line is \(b_1^{\mathrm{bd}},b_2^{\mathrm{bd}},b_4^{\mathrm{bd}}\); the two rays therefore meet only at \(b_2^{\mathrm{bd}}\).  All endpoints are fixed, and (14) fixes every coefficient.  In particular, the four displayed zeros are compulsory and
\[
 \tau_C=
 \left(0+\frac16+\frac13,
       \frac13+\frac16+0\right)
 =\left(\frac12,\frac12\right). \tag{21}
\]
The rank-two atlas and the target-preserving lift prove the asserted singleton target set.

On the relative support face preserving those four zero positions, positivity of every other coefficient and endpoint, strict endpoint order, transversality, and \(m\ne r\) are strict relative inequalities.  The displayed datum satisfies all of them, so the chart is nonempty.  The same intersection-and-ray argument proves rigidity throughout it.  Finally, \(S=1\) almost surely would imply \(P(E\mid S=1)=P(E)\), hence \(r=m\).  Since \(r^{\mathrm{bd}}\ne m^{\mathrm{bd}}\), the boundary datum is outside the 2023 experimental conditions.

Fix \(\vartheta\in\mathcal F_B(p)\) in the stated no-selection overlap and suppose \(\mathcal K_{\mathrm K}(P_{\vartheta})\).  The cited Kawakami theorem applies because \(\mathcal K_{\mathrm K}\) records its recursive factorization, all required invertibilities, the cross-treatment separation, and the two structural exclusions.  Its simultaneous equations identify \(\omega_0^{\mathrm K}\) and \(\omega_1^{\mathrm K}\).

In the order \((00,01,10,11)\), response consistency says that \((X,Y)=(1,1)\) admits exactly types \(01\) and \(11\), while \((X,Y)=(0,0)\) admits exactly types \(00\) and \(01\).  Positive observed cells and \(S=1\) almost surely make both conditioning events positive.  Bayes' rule therefore gives
\[
 \mathrm{PN}(\vartheta)
 =\frac{\omega^{\mathrm K}_{1,2}}
        {\omega^{\mathrm K}_{1,2}+\omega^{\mathrm K}_{1,4}},
 \qquad
 \mathrm{PS}(\vartheta)
 =\frac{\omega^{\mathrm K}_{0,2}}
        {\omega^{\mathrm K}_{0,1}+\omega^{\mathrm K}_{0,2}}. \tag{22}
\]
By definition of \(\phi_{\mathrm K}\),
\[
 \tau(\vartheta)
 =\phi_{\mathrm K}(\omega_0^{\mathrm K},\omega_1^{\mathrm K}). \tag{23}
\]
If \(\mathcal T_B(p)\) is a singleton, it contains \(\tau(\vartheta)\) by definition.  The full-rigidity theorem returns its unique member, and hence the value in (23).  The cited theorem identifies the four binary potential-outcome-type probabilities as well as the treatment-conditional weights used in (22), proving the asserted overlap scope.

For the separate scope witness, every row of \(A_x^{\mathrm K}(b^{\mathrm{bd}})\) is
\[
 \bigl(1,b_i^{\mathrm{bd}}(w_1),
          b_i^{\mathrm{bd}}(w_2),b_i^{\mathrm{bd}}(w_3)\bigr). \tag{24}
\]
Because \(b_i^{\mathrm{bd}}\) is a probability vector on three points, the last three entries in (24) sum to one.  Thus the first column of \(A_x^{\mathrm K}(b^{\mathrm{bd}})\) is the sum of its last three columns, for each \(x\), and
\[
 \det A_x^{\mathrm K}(b^{\mathrm{bd}})=0. \tag{25}
\]
The experimental-overlap and boundary-separation theorem proves
\[
 \mathcal F_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})\ne\varnothing,
 \qquad
 \mathcal T_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})
 =\{(1/2,1/2)\}. \tag{26}
\]
Hence this legal selected response-cycle law is exactly classified by the atlas, but (25) violates the invertibility premise in Kawakami's Theorem 1(i).  The single explicit law proves strict scope separation and makes no subsumption claim.

Let \(k=|\mathcal Z|\) and \(\ell=|\mathcal W|\).  In design A, the four endpoint vectors \(b_i\) contribute \(4\ell\) variables and the two incident coefficient vectors in each of four cells contribute \(8k\), so
\[
 N_A=4\ell+8k. \tag{27}
\]
Endpoint nonnegativity and normalization use \(4\ell+4\) sign atoms, coefficient nonnegativity uses \(8k\), the four equations \(a_{ei}+a_{ej}=v_e\) use \(4k\), and the factorization equations use \(4k\ell\).  Hence
\[
 S_A=4k\ell+4\ell+12k+4. \tag{28}
\]
Only the factorization equations are nonlinear, and they are bilinear in \((b,a)\); therefore \(D_A=2\).

The design-B presentation adds four margin coordinates, \(k\) common-instrument coordinates, and four response-mass coordinates.  Thus
\[
 N_B=N_A+4+k+4=4\ell+9k+8. \tag{29}
\]
Margin positivity and normalization add five atoms, common-instrument positivity and normalization add \(k+1\), response-mass nonnegativity and normalization add five, and the shared-\(Z\) equations add \(4k\).  Relevance is the disjunction, over distinct \(z,z'\), of the signs of
\[
 q^X_zg(z')-q^X_{z'}g(z). \tag{30}
\]
Using the conservative allowance \(2k(k-1)\) for these sign atoms and adding to (28) gives
\[
 S_B\le 4k\ell+2k^2+4\ell+15k+15. \tag{31}
\]
The shared-\(Z\) equations are quadratic.  Since \(q^X_z\) is bilinear in \((m,a)\), (30) is cubic, and no raw atom has larger degree; hence \(D_B=3\).  The unequal-target atom has degree two because \(\tau_C\) is linear, so it does not increase either raw degree bound.

Apply the established effective semialgebraic sampling theorem once to the raw design-\(d\) fiber over \(K=\mathbb K_{\zeta}\).  It generates at most \(A_{S,d}\) records.  If the fiber is nonempty, write \(\xi\) for a primitive element of the returned representation of \(x_0\).  Then
\[
 [K(\xi):K]\le D_{S,d}. \tag{32}
\]
Every coordinate of \(x_0\) lies in \(K(\xi)\).  Since \(t_0=\tau_C(x_0)\) consists of linear sums of those coordinates,
\[
 K(t_0)\subseteq K(\xi),
 \qquad [K(t_0):K]\le D_{S,d}. \tag{33}
\]
This proves, separately, that every initial-sample coordinate and each rigid target coordinate has degree at most \(D_{S,d}\) over \(K\).

There is one existential-realizability call over \(K(t_0)\) on the raw fiber plus the unequal-target atom.  It generates at most \(A_{E,d}\) records.  If it returns a witness \(x_1\) with primitive element \(\upsilon\), then
\[
 [K(t_0,\upsilon):K(t_0)]\le D_{E,d}. \tag{34}
\]
The tower law and (33)--(34) yield
\[
 [K(t_0,\upsilon):K]
 =[K(t_0,\upsilon):K(t_0)][K(t_0):K]
 \le D_{S,d}D_{E,d}. \tag{35}
\]
Every coordinate of \(x_1\), but not necessarily every coordinate of \(x_0\), lies in the field in (35).  In any extension of degree at most \(D\), the \(D+1\) elements \(1,u,\ldots,u^D\) are linearly dependent over the base field, so every element \(u\) has minimal-polynomial degree at most \(D\).  Consequently the initial and second-stage coordinate degrees are bounded respectively by \(D_{S,d}\) and \(D_{S,d}D_{E,d}\), and their maximum is exactly the stated \(\mathcal D_{k,\ell}\).  This is the required separation of the two representations; it does not place \(x_0\) inside \(K(t_0,\upsilon)\).

The two fixed status/output records and the two algorithmic record bounds give
\[
 R_{k,\ell}=2+
 \max_{d\in\{A,B\}}(A_{S,d}+A_{E,d}). \tag{36}
\]
The established mixed-support theorem independently gives the diagnostic counts
\[
 M_A=(2^{\ell}-1)^4(3^{k+1}+3)^4,
 \qquad
 M_B=M_Ak(k-1)(2k-1)^4. \tag{37}
\]
They do not enter (32)--(36), because each algorithmic call is made directly on one raw fiber.

Put \(Q=k\ell+k^2+\ell+1\).  Equations (27)--(31) imply, after enlarging a universal constant \(C\),
\[
 N_d\le CQ,
 \qquad S_d\le CQ,
 \qquad D_d\le3. \tag{38}
\]
The coordinatewise nondecreasing bounds in the effective semialgebraic theorem therefore give
\[
 A_{S,d},D_{S,d},A_{E,d},D_{E,d}
 \le 2^{CQ^C}. \tag{39}
\]
Substitution into (35)--(36), with one further enlargement of \(C\), proves
\[
 R_{k,\ell}\le2^{CQ^C},
 \qquad
 \mathcal D_{k,\ell}\le2^{CQ^C}. \tag{40}
\]
For arbitrary real input, selected-table positivity makes every \(r_e\) strictly positive, so the observable divisions defining \(T_e\) and \(v_e\) are legal and all raw coefficients lie in \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\).  The effective field arithmetic, order, sign, sampling, and real-root procedures in the cited result terminate, proving relative termination.

Now suppose the rational input numerators and denominators have binary length at most \(L\).  Reconstructing deleted simplex coordinates, forming \(r_e\), passing to \(T_e\) and \(v_e\), and clearing those guarded observable denominators in degree-at-most-three atoms requires only a quadratic number of rational sums and products in \(Q\).  Thus
\[
 h_0=64Q^2(L+1) \tag{41}
\]
is a conservative bound for all cleared integer input coefficients.  The cited height bounds give \(h_{S,d}\) for the representation of \(x_0\), and then \(h_{E,d}\) for the relative second-stage representation over \(K(t_0)\).  A coordinate of \(t_0\) is a sum of at most \(k\) initial coordinates, so \(c_k=\lceil\log_2(k+1)\rceil+1\) conservatively absorbs the extra addition height.

Apply tower flattening separately.  The initial sample and its target use extension degree at most \(D_{S,d}\) and height input at most \(h_0+h_{S,d}+c_k\), giving \(h_{F,0,d}\).  The second witness uses the product degree in (35) and combined height input at most \(h_0+h_{S,d}+h_{E,d}+c_k\), giving \(h_{F,1,d}\).  Square-free factorization and rational root isolation preserve the degree bounds and are included in these two \(\mathsf{Flat}_h\) envelopes.  Therefore the maximum \(H_{k,\ell}(L)\) dominates both the separately flattened \(x_0\) representation and the second-stage representation.

Finally, the height clause of the effective semialgebraic theorem, coordinatewise monotonicity of the sampling and existential bounds, (38), and the explicit sequential arguments just given imply, after enlarging \(C\),
\[
 H_{k,\ell}(L)
 \le \bigl[64Q^2(L+2)\bigr]^{2^{CQ^C}}. \tag{42}
\]
This is a height bound separate from the singly exponential record and degree bounds in (40).  Every subroutine is finite on rational data, so the rational-input Turing implementation terminates.  Equations (32)--(42) prove the corrected theorem without a chart multiplier, connected-component computation, target projection, or two-copy classifier.

Fix a compact set \(H\subset\mathfrak R_{\varepsilon}\).  All uniform statements below are over \(\zeta\in H\).  The reduced selected-table coordinates are averages of bounded categorical vectors.  When design-A margins are estimated, their reduced coordinates come from an independent sample and \(n/n_m\to\lambda\in(0,\infty)\).  Hence, for some finite \(C_H\),
\[
 \sup_{\zeta\in H}
 E_{\zeta}\|\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta\|_2^2
 \le \frac{C_H}{n}. \tag{43}
\]
The margin term is absent when margins are known.  Markov's inequality yields
\[
 \widehat\zeta_n-\zeta=O_P(n^{-1/2}) \tag{44}
\]
uniformly on \(H\).

The selected-table covariance is \(\operatorname{diag}(p^-)-p^-p^{-\top}\).  Independence and proportional sample-size scaling add the block
\(\lambda\{\operatorname{diag}(m^-)-m^-m^{-\top}\}\) when margins are estimated.  These are precisely the blocks of \(\Omega_{\zeta}\).  The established multinomial central-limit and delta lemma gives
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta)
 \Rightarrow N(0,\Omega_{\zeta}). \tag{45}
\]
The convergence is uniform on \(H\): for any sequence in \(H\), compactness supplies a convergent subsequence, and bounded categorical summands satisfy the Lindeberg condition uniformly along it; the subsequence criterion then proves uniformity.  Since the covariance formula is continuous in the cell probabilities, (44) and continuous mapping also give
\[
 \widehat\Omega_n\xrightarrow{P}\Omega_{\zeta} \tag{46}
\]
uniformly.

For each \(\zeta\in H\), the incident set
\[
 \Gamma(\zeta)=
 \{\chi:d_{\chi}(\zeta)=0,\ \eta_{\chi}(\zeta)\ge\varepsilon\} \tag{47}
\]
is nonempty.  Distance to a closed set is one-Lipschitz, so an incident \(\chi\) obeys
\[
 d_{\chi}(\widehat\zeta_n)
 \le\|\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta\|_2. \tag{48}
\]
There are finitely many labels, and the required slack extensions are continuous.  A compactness and finite-subcover argument therefore supplies \(\delta_H>0\) such that, for at least one \(\chi\in\Gamma(\zeta)\),
\[
 \|\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta\|_2<\delta_H
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \eta_{\chi}(\widehat\zeta_n)\ge\varepsilon/2. \tag{49}
\]
Because \(t_n=n^{-1/4}\) and (44) is of order \(n^{-1/2}\), (48)--(49) show that some incident chart passes both selector inequalities with probability tending uniformly to one.

Every incompatible chart closure is at distance at least \(\varepsilon\) from \(\zeta\).  For such a chart,
\[
 d_{\chi}(\widehat\zeta_n)
 \ge\varepsilon-\|\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta\|_2. \tag{50}
\]
On the event where the norm is below \(\varepsilon/2\), the right side exceeds \(t_n\) for all large \(n\).  Thus no incompatible chart passes.  Exhaustive certification and lexicographic selection imply
\[
 \sup_{\zeta\in H}P_{\zeta}
 \{\widehat\chi_n=\bot\ \text{or }\widehat\chi_n
 \text{ is not incident and first-order compatible}\}
 \longrightarrow0. \tag{51}
\]

On the complementary event, rigidity and first-order compatibility give
\[
 F_{\widehat\chi_n}(\zeta)=\tau,
 \qquad
 J_{\widehat\chi_n}(\zeta)=J(\zeta), \tag{52}
\]
where \(J(\zeta)\) is the common incident Jacobian.  The twice continuously differentiable extensions, finiteness of the chart set, and compactness yield a common Hessian bound.  Taylor's theorem and (44) give
\[
 \widehat\tau_n-\tau
 =J(\zeta)(\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta)+R_n,
 \qquad
 \sqrt n\|R_n\|_2=o_P(1) \tag{53}
\]
uniformly.  Combining (45) and (53) proves
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat\tau_n-\tau)
 \Rightarrow N(0,J(\zeta)\Omega_{\zeta}J(\zeta)^{\top})
 =N(0,V_{\tau}). \tag{54}
\]

Continuity of the chart derivatives, (44), and (46) imply
\[
 J_{\widehat\chi_n}(\widehat\zeta_n)\widehat\Omega_n
 J_{\widehat\chi_n}(\widehat\zeta_n)^{\top}
 \xrightarrow{P}V_{\tau} \tag{55}
\]
uniformly.  Since \(\lambda_{\min}(V_{\tau})\ge\varepsilon\), continuity of eigenvalues makes the matrix in (55) positive definite with probability tending uniformly to one.  Therefore \(\widehat\gamma_n=1\) with probability tending to one and
\(\widehat V_n\xrightarrow{P}V_{\tau}\).

For every fixed nonzero contrast \(h\), Slutsky's lemma gives
\[
 \frac{\sqrt n\,h^{\top}(\widehat\tau_n-\tau)}
 {(h^{\top}\widehat V_nh)^{1/2}}
 \Rightarrow N(0,1). \tag{56}
\]
Likewise,
\[
 n(\widehat\tau_n-\tau)^{\top}\widehat V_n^{-1}
 (\widehat\tau_n-\tau)\Rightarrow\chi^2_2. \tag{57}
\]
The true target is in \([0,1]^2\), so intersecting the ellipse with that square leaves its coverage event unchanged.  Continuity at the displayed normal and chi-square quantiles proves asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\) for scalar contrasts and the ellipse.

If no chart is certified, the definitions give \(\widehat\chi_n=\bot\), \(F_{\bot}=(0,0)\), and \(J_{\bot}=0\).  The raw sandwich is then zero and is not positive definite, so
\[
 \widehat\gamma_n=0,
 \qquad \widehat\tau_n=(0,0),
 \qquad \widehat V_n=I_2,
 \qquad W_n=[0,1]^2. \tag{58}
\]
The consistency and Wald conclusions above used the high-probability event in (51); no such assertion is made on this fallback branch.

Let \(q_0\) be the true observable law, including the independent margin law when design-A margins are estimated, and put \(t_0=\tau(\vartheta)\).  Each selected-table count and each applicable margin count has a binomial marginal law.  By direct inversion of the two binomial tails, each Clopper--Pearson interval has at least its allocated marginal coverage.  The stated Bonferroni allocation therefore gives
\[
 P_{q_0}\{q_0\notin C_n\}\le\beta_n. \tag{59}
\]

For fixed compatible \((q,t)\), define the exact nonrandomized upper-tail value
\[
 G_{q,t}=P_q\{\Delta_n^{\mathrm{rep}}(t)
                   \ge\Delta_n^{\mathrm{obs}}(t)\}.
\]
It is super-uniform.  Indeed, order the finite support of \(\Delta_n(t)\).  For \(u\in[0,1]\), let \(d\) be the least support point whose upper-tail probability is at most \(u\), if such a point exists.  Then
\(\{G_{q,t}\le u\}\subseteq\{\Delta_n^{\mathrm{obs}}(t)\ge d\}\), whence
\[
 P_q\{G_{q,t}\le u\}\le u. \tag{60}
\]
If no such \(d\) exists, the event on the left is empty.

Compatibility gives \(t_0\in\mathcal T(q_0)\).  On \(\{q_0\in C_n\}\), the supremum defining the calibrated value includes \(q_0\), so
\[
 \operatorname{pv}_n(t_0)
 \ge\min\{1,\beta_n+G_{q_0,t_0}\}. \tag{61}
\]
Because \(\beta_n\le\alpha/2<\alpha\), (59)--(61) imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_{q_0}\{t_0\notin K_n\}
 &\le P_{q_0}\{q_0\notin C_n\}
   +P_{q_0}\{G_{q_0,t_0}\le\alpha-\beta_n\}\\
 &\le\beta_n+(\alpha-\beta_n)=\alpha.
 \end{aligned} \tag{62}
\]
This argument is finite-sample and pointwise.  Applying it at each element of any triangular sequence proves the same coverage near \(\mathfrak D\), including point-to-set transitions, without a rank, support, or boundary limit condition.

For the Hausdorff assertion, restrict attention to a compact subset satisfying the stated local-saturation hypotheses.  Positivity and compactness bound every local multinomial cell probability away from zero.  Since eventually \(\beta_n=n^{-2}\), binomial Chernoff bounds inverted at these tails, followed by a finite union bound, give
\[
 \sup_{q\in C_n}\|q-q_0\|_2
 =O_P\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}\right)=o_P(1) \tag{63}
\]
uniformly.  For example, exponential Markov inequality at the optimizing Bernoulli tilt gives
\(P_p(\widehat p\ge x)\le e^{-nD(x\Vert p)}\); since
\(\partial_x^2D(x\Vert p)=1/\{x(1-x)\}\ge4\) and both the divergence and its first derivative vanish at \(x=p\),
\(D(x\Vert p)\ge2(x-p)^2\).  The lower tail is symmetric.  This proves (63) directly.  With probability tending to one, every law in the calibration supremum is therefore inside the common saturated neighborhood, where compatibility holds and \(t\in\mathcal T(q)\) is equivalent to \(t=F(q)\).

Write \(z\) for reduced coordinates and \(\widehat z\) for their unrestricted multinomial maximum-likelihood estimator.  On the positive compact neighborhood, a third-order Taylor expansion of the finite multinomial likelihood, uniformly for \(z-\widehat z=O(n^{-1/2})\), gives
\[
 2\{\ell_n(\widehat z)-\ell_n(z)\}
 =n(z-\widehat z)^{\top}\Omega_{\zeta}^{-1}
       (z-\widehat z)+o_P(1). \tag{64}
\]
For two independent samples, the proportional scaling gives the two blocks in \(\Omega_{\zeta}\).  The inverse exists in reduced coordinates because all local probabilities are positive.

Let \(J=\partial F(\zeta)/\partial\zeta^{\top}\).  Twice continuous differentiability yields
\[
 F(z)-F(\widehat z)
 =J(z-\widehat z)+O(\|z-\widehat z\|_2^2). \tag{65}
\]
Strict concavity of the interior multinomial likelihood and compactness give a positive Kullback--Leibler gap outside the fixed local neighborhood, so every constrained maximizer for a bounded root-\(n\) target displacement is local with probability tending uniformly to one.

Minimizing the quadratic form in (64) under the linearized constraint in (65), the Lagrange first-order condition gives
\[
 z-\widehat z
 =\Omega_{\zeta}J^{\top}
   (J\Omega_{\zeta}J^{\top})^{-1}
   (t-\widehat\tau_n).
\]
Since \(\lambda_{\min}(V_{\tau})\ge\varepsilon\), the inverse exists and the minimizer is unique.  Substitution gives
\[
 \Delta_n(t)
 =n(t-\widehat\tau_n)^{\top}V_{\tau}^{-1}
       (t-\widehat\tau_n)+o_P(1) \tag{66}
\]
uniformly for bounded \(\sqrt n\|t-\widehat\tau_n\|_2\); the Kullback--Leibler gap makes the discrepancy diverge outside a bounded local target set.

Apply the same expansions to independent replicates, uniformly over the shrinking set in (63), and use the finite-alphabet central limit theorem together with covariance consistency from the separated-Wald theorem.  Then
\[
 \sup_{q\in C_n:\,t=F(q)}
 \left|
 P_q\{\Delta_n^{\mathrm{rep}}(t)\ge\Delta_n^{\mathrm{obs}}(t)\}
 -\overline F_{\chi^2_2}\!\left(
 n(t-\widehat\tau_n)^{\top}\widehat V_n^{-1}
 (t-\widehat\tau_n)\right)
 \right|=o_P(1). \tag{67}
\]
Positive definiteness of \(V_{\tau}\) implies that \(J\) has row rank two.  Because the local map \(F\) takes a full neighborhood into \([0,1]^2\), the submersion theorem then forces \(F(\zeta)\) to be an interior point of the square; otherwise its image could not contain a relative Euclidean neighborhood.  Thus truncation by the square is locally inactive.

The chi-square distribution is continuous and \(\beta_n=o(1)\).  Equation (67) sandwiches \(K_n\), with probability tending to one, between ellipsoids obtained by perturbing \(\chi^2_{2,1-\alpha}\) by \(\pm\delta_n\), where \(\delta_n=o_P(1)\).  The eigenvalues of \(\widehat V_n\) are uniformly bounded above and away from zero, so radial comparison yields
\[
 d_{\mathrm H}(K_n,W_n)
 \le n^{-1/2}O_P(\delta_n)=o_P(n^{-1/2}). \tag{68}
\]
This proves the compact-uniform Hausdorff conclusion.  Without singleton local saturation, chart separation, and nonsingularity, (64)--(68) need not hold; the universally valid conclusion is only the finite-sample coverage in (62).

Selected-table positivity gives \(r_e>0\), \(T_e(w,z)>0\), and
\[
 v_e(z)=\sum_wT_e(w,z)>0 \tag{69}
\]
for every \(e,z\).  Fix a cell with \(\mathcal I_e=\{i,j\}\).  Every legal cycle point satisfies
\[
 T_e=b_i a_{ei}^{\top}+b_j a_{ej}^{\top},
 \qquad a_{ei}+a_{ej}=v_e. \tag{70}
\]
The first right side is a sum of two rank-one matrices, so \(\operatorname{rank}(T_e)\le2\); positivity excludes rank zero.  Thus rank above two makes both cycle fibers empty.

If \(\operatorname{rank}(T_e)=2\), define the legal normalized columns
\(c_{ez}=T_e(\cdot,z)/v_e(z)\).  Equation (70) becomes
\[
 c_{ez}=\lambda_{ez}b_i+(1-\lambda_{ez})b_j,
 \qquad
 \lambda_{ez}=\frac{a_{ei}(z)}{v_e(z)}\in[0,1]. \tag{71}
\]
Rank two forces \(b_i\ne b_j\).  Conversely, any two endpoints on the observed affine line whose closed segment contains all \(c_{ez}\) determine, for a coordinate \(h_e\) with \(b_i(h_e)\ne b_j(h_e)\),
\[
 a_{ei}(z)=v_e(z)
 \frac{c_{ez}(h_e)-b_j(h_e)}{b_i(h_e)-b_j(h_e)},
 \qquad
 a_{ej}(z)=v_e(z)-a_{ei}(z). \tag{72}
\]
The recorded pivot is nonzero, and the segment inequalities make both coefficients nonnegative.  Endpoint reversal gives the second orientation.  For each \(z\), the positive sum in (70) has precisely three support alternatives: the first coefficient is zero, the second is zero, or both are positive.  Hence the two orientations and their coordinatewise support refinements exhaust the rank-two cell.

If \(\operatorname{rank}(T_e)=1\), the established rank-one normal-form lemma supplies the unique positive column point and proves that the \(\mathrm L,\mathrm R,\mathrm E,\mathrm D\) modes are disjoint and exhaustive.  Its coordinatewise refinement of \(\mathrm E\) retains the three alternatives \(s_e(z)=0\), \(0<s_e(z)<v_e(z)\), and \(s_e(z)=v_e(z)\).  Therefore inactive rows, equal endpoints, and every forced-zero face are included without division.

Take the product of the four local lists and identify the two occurrences of each response endpoint \(b_i\).  Endpoint simplex and support conditions, endpoint equalities or inequalities, observed-line incidence, segment order, and (70)--(72) become polynomial sign conditions after a denominator is cleared only on the chart recording its nonzero sign.  The exhaustive alternatives above show that every point of \(\mathcal C_A(T)\) enters at least one chart.  Conversely, substitution of any chart point in (70), together with its simplex and support conditions, proves cycle-fiber membership.  Thus
\[
 \bigcup_{\chi}X^A_{\chi}=\mathcal C_A(T). \tag{73}
\]

For design B, fix a design-A cycle point and a positive projective coordinate \(\rho\).  The established residual-forest theorem proves that, at every response type, either both incident residuals vanish or they are nonzero and negatively proportional; exactly one vanishing residual is infeasible.  In an active state, the first nonzero residual coordinate supplies a lexicographic pivot and its sign supplies a finite refinement.  Positive margin ratios propagate from one positive scale on each forest component, and an active cycle is consistent precisely when the product of its ratios is one.  Normalization fixes the remaining common scale.  Finally relevance is the finite disjunction
\[
 q^X_zg(z')-q^X_{z'}g(z)>0
 \quad\text{or}\quad
 q^X_zg(z')-q^X_{z'}g(z)<0 \tag{74}
\]
over unordered distinct pairs.  By the necessary-and-sufficient residual-forest theorem, these states exhaust positive margins, the shared-\(Z\) equations, and relevance.  Hence
\[
 \bigcup_{\chi}X^B_{\chi}=\mathcal C_B(T). \tag{75}
\]

There are \(2^{\ell}-1\) nonempty support labels for each of the four endpoints, giving \((2^{\ell}-1)^4\) shared endpoint-support patterns.  A rank-two local library has \(2\cdot3^k\) oriented support modes.  A rank-one library has \(3^k\) refined \(\mathrm E\) modes and the three additional modes \(\mathrm L,\mathrm R,\mathrm D\).  Before observed rank is consulted, the local total is therefore at most
\[
 2\cdot3^k+3^k+3=3^{k+1}+3. \tag{76}
\]
Multiplying its fourth power by the endpoint-support count gives \(M_A\).  In design B, each of the four response links has one zero-residual state or \(2(k-1)\) active pivot-and-sign states, giving \((2k-1)^4\).  The unordered relevance pair and its sign have \(2\binom{k}{2}=k(k-1)\) labels.  This proves the stated \(M_B\).

Every coefficient in these sign conditions is obtained from \(T\) and \(v\).  Since \(T_e=p_e/r_e\) and \(r_e>0\), all coefficients lie in \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\).  Equations (71)--(75) include every zero-support and coincident-endpoint face, proving exact field-tier exhaustiveness.  The atlas may therefore label a raw-fiber result, but it is not used by the direct rigidity decision.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For fixed \(k=|\mathcal Z|\) and \(\ell=|\mathcal W|\), the raw design-A fiber has a polynomial presentation with
\[
 N_A=4\ell+8k,
 \qquad
 S_A=4k\ell+4\ell+12k+4,
 \qquad
 D_A=2,
\]
and the raw design-B fiber has one with
\[
 N_B=4\ell+9k+8,
 \qquad
 S_B=4k\ell+2k^2+4\ell+15k+15,
 \qquad
 D_B=3.
\]
For \(d\in\{A,B\}\), let
\[
 (A_{S,d},D_{S,d})=\mathsf{Samp}(N_d,S_d,D_d),
 \qquad
 (A_{E,d},D_{E,d})=\mathsf{Exist}(N_d,S_d+1,D_d),
\]
where the second bound is relative to the finite real algebraic coefficient extension generated by the initial target.  Define
\[
 R_{k,\ell}=2+\max_{d\in\{A,B\}}(A_{S,d}+A_{E,d}),
 \qquad
 \mathcal D_{k,\ell}=
 \max_{d\in\{A,B\}}\max\{D_{S,d},D_{S,d}D_{E,d}\}.
\]
The mandatory raw-fiber engine makes at most one sampling call and, on a nonempty fiber, one unequal-target existential call.  Its algebraic record count is at most \(R_{k,\ell}\).  Every initial-sample or rigid-target coordinate has algebraic degree at most \(D_{S,d}\) over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), while every second-stage witness coordinate has degree at most \(D_{S,d}D_{E,d}\); consequently every returned coordinate has degree at most \(\mathcal D_{k,\ell}\).  No assertion is made that the initial sample lies in the field generated by the initial target and the second-stage primitive element.

The separate diagnostic structural atlas has at most
\[
 M_A=(2^{\ell}-1)^4(3^{k+1}+3)^4,
 \qquad
 M_B=M_Ak(k-1)(2k-1)^4
\]
templates, but neither number multiplies \(R_{k,\ell}\) or \(\mathcal D_{k,\ell}\).  If \(Q=k\ell+k^2+\ell+1\), there is a universal constant \(C\ge1\), independent of \(k\), \(\ell\), and the input, such that
\[
 R_{k,\ell}\le 2^{CQ^C},
 \qquad
 \mathcal D_{k,\ell}\le 2^{CQ^C}.
\]

Over an arbitrary real input field \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), the computation terminates relative to effective field arithmetic, order, sign-determination, and real-root oracles.  For rational input coordinates of binary length at most \(L\), put
\[
 h_0=64Q^2(L+1),
 \qquad
 h_{S,d}=\mathsf{Samp}_h(N_d,S_d,D_d,h_0),
\]
\[
 h_{E,d}=\mathsf{Exist}_h
 (N_d,S_d+1,D_d;h_0,h_{S,d},D_{S,d}),
\]
and, writing \(c_k=\lceil\log_2(k+1)\rceil+1\), define the two separate flattening bounds
\[
 h_{F,0,d}=\mathsf{Flat}_h(D_{S,d},h_0+h_{S,d}+c_k),
 \qquad
 h_{F,1,d}=\mathsf{Flat}_h
 (D_{S,d}D_{E,d},h_0+h_{S,d}+h_{E,d}+c_k).
\]
Let
\[
 H_{k,\ell}(L)=
 \max_{d\in\{A,B\}}\max\{h_{S,d},h_{E,d},h_{F,0,d},h_{F,1,d}\}.
\]
After flattening each initial representation separately from any second-stage representation, and clearing only guarded denominators, every algebraic target or witness coordinate has a square-free integer polynomial of degree at most \(\mathcal D_{k,\ell}\) and rational isolating data of binary length at most \(H_{k,\ell}(L)\).  After enlarging the same universal constant if necessary,
\[
 H_{k,\ell}(L)
 \le \bigl[64Q^2(L+2)\bigr]^{2^{CQ^C}}.
\]
Thus record count and algebraic degree have singly exponential fixed-alphabet bounds, while rational height has the separate displayed bound.  A rational-input Turing implementation terminates.  The mandatory decision neither enumerates structural charts nor computes connected components or a target projection, and it uses no generic two-copy latent classifier.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The frozen statement still counts chart-by-chart calls and does not separate the initial sample field from the second-stage witness field. The accepted raw-fiber engine uses one sampling call and one existential call. Its initial coordinates have the sampling degree bound in their own primitive extension, whereas only a second-stage witness has the product extension-degree bound. The corrected claim takes the maximum of those bounds and separately flattens both rational representations.

prose_updates.tldr: For every fixed finite four-response-type selected proxy model, PN/PS rigidity is decided directly on the raw legal cycle fiber. After the strict supplied-margin check in design A, the compiler makes one bounded-algebraic-sampling call and, when the fiber is nonempty, one one-copy unequal-target existential call. It returns incompatibility, an exact common target, or legal same-observable SCM twins. A separate exhaustive rank-two, rank-one-mode, support-face, shared-endpoint, and relevant-IV residual-forest atlas supplies optional structural labels but is not queried by the decision engine. The initial sample and a possible second-stage witness are represented and flattened separately; their degree bounds are respectively the sampling bound and the product of the sequential extension bounds. The published regular formulas retain their existing transfer scope, fixed-alphabet record and algebraic-degree bounds are singly exponential, rational height has a separate conservative bound, and the accepted Wald, exact-coverage, and locally saturated Hausdorff qualifications are unchanged.

project_justification.niche: The four response types form a labeled causal cycle whose target can be rigid while nuisance factorizations vary. The normalized design-A and design-B legal fibers are themselves bounded one-copy semialgebraic sets, so global constancy is decided by comparing every feasible point with one sampled target in a single existential query. The exhaustive orientation, rank-one, support-face, shared-endpoint, and residual-forest charts remain a separate exact explanation of every singular and boundary configuration.
project_justification.fill: The compiler first checks strict supplied-margin compatibility in design A, samples once from the applicable raw legal fiber, and performs one raw-fiber unequal-target test. It returns an exact target, legal target-changing full SCMs, or incompatibility. The separate structural atlas can label the result and retains its finite template bound, but contributes no multiplier or auxiliary variables to mandatory decision complexity. The termination theorem uses raw polynomial degree two in design A and degree three in design B. It bounds the initial sample in its own sampling extension, bounds a second-stage witness by the product of the sequential extension degrees, takes their maximum, and flattens the two rational representations separately. Rational height is reported separately.

prose_updates.related_work: Shingaki, Yoshida, and Kuroki (2026) supply the selected response-type factorization and the regular identification results used here. At the selected-law factorization level, the present finite four-type model specializes their Condition 1. The fixed-margin two-proxy fiber is a restriction to which Theorem 1 applies, while the relevant-IV fiber satisfies equation (13) and relevance, so Corollary 1 applies directly. Our contribution does not extend their regular formula or subsume their model; it classifies additional compatible singular and boundary fibers and reports incompatible inputs separately. Shingaki and Kuroki (2023) and Kawakami (2021) provide separate experimental and IV-plus-proxy overlap results under their own conditions. Nonnegative-factorization rigidity work supplies geometric context but not causal target constancy on this labeled response cycle. Basu, Pollack, and Roy (2006) supply the exact bounded-algebraic-sampling, existential-realizability, real-univariate, sign, and root-isolation algorithms used by the two-call raw-fiber engine and, optionally, by structural diagnostics.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The result is a theorem-level exact symbolic procedure, not a claim of a completed production implementation or favorable growing-alphabet complexity. The mandatory decision works on the raw legal fiber and makes at most one sampling and one unequal-target existential call. The finite structural atlas can be produced diagnostically but is not required for compatibility or rigidity. Over arbitrary real observables, computation is relative to effective coefficient-field arithmetic, order, sign-determination, and real-root oracles. The initial sample need not belong to the field generated by its target and a second-stage primitive element; it is bounded and flattened in its own sampling extension. A rational expression is returned only when constructed; otherwise the result remains a real-univariate and Thom encoding. The singly exponential statement covers fixed-alphabet record count and algebraic degree only; rational coefficient and isolating-endpoint height obey the separate displayed power bound. Strictly positive twins require both cycle witnesses to lie in interior support charts. The accepted exact-coverage and locally saturated Hausdorff qualifications are unchanged. The released numerical GEUVADIS count table and binarization thresholds remain unavailable in the frozen materials, so no numerical dataset verdict is asserted.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The mathematical contribution is an exact fixed-alphabet raw-fiber rigidity decision together with a separate exhaustive response-cycle structural atlas. Design-A margins outside the strict interior and empty raw fibers are reported as incompatibility, which is non-rigid under the cardinality-one definition. One raw-fiber sample and one unequal-target existential query decide global constancy across all components and support faces; the chart atlas supplies optional diagnoses rather than a computational prerequisite. The regular two-proxy result transfers only by restricting Condition 1 to a fixed population margin, and the regular IV result transfers through equation (13) and Corollary 1; the new result adds compatible singular and boundary classification, not a new regular formula or blanket subsumption. Initial-sample coordinates receive their own sampling-extension degree bound, second-stage coordinates receive the product extension-degree bound, and separately flattened representations are covered by their maximum. Record count and normalized algebraic degree receive singly exponential fixed-alphabet bounds, while rational height receives a separate conservative bound. The statistical Wald, exact-coverage, and locally saturated Hausdorff scopes remain unchanged. The GEUVADIS application remains an audit protocol conditional on the graph and recovery of the actual released table, not a new numerical reanalysis.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem bounds the actual two-call raw-fiber engine and separately controls the initial sampling extension and the second-stage product extension before taking their maximum.
statement_notes.gap: Chart counts and residual-forest auxiliaries belong to optional diagnostics, and the initial sample cannot generally be placed in the field generated only by its target and a later witness primitive element.
statement_notes.consumer: Exact implementations receive raw degree two for design A, raw degree three for design B, no chart multiplier, separate initial and second-stage degree bounds, and a separately composed rational-height guarantee.
